# Bridge native image enhancement with binary payloads and an original-image fallback

## Platform difference

An OH-only image-enhancement service needs explicit availability, data transfer and fallback handling around ordinary Flutter image rendering.

## Implementation

Venera moves image bytes to BasicMessageChannel/BinaryCodec, keeps a separate availability probe, and handles timeout/null-cache cases. It then shows the original image while precaching the enhanced result. A later opt-in ArkTS local reader provides an alternative native rendering route rather than forcing every Flutter page into ArkUI.

## Applicability

The native service is device/product/API dependent. Channel presence only establishes that a handler exists, not that enhancement is available, correct or fast on every device.

These observations apply to the pinned project revisions below, studied on 2026-09-30 and backfilled on 2026-10-06. Unspecified SDK/device compatibility remains unknown; this is not a fresh upstream assessment.

## Pitfalls and limitations

Do not claim zero-copy or performance improvements from a codec choice alone. A timeout must leave usable original content and avoid stale results replacing newer pages. The native reader is experimental and optional in this branch.

## Verification

Test unavailable service, large images, cancellation/page changes, timeout, cache invalidation and visual quality/performance with original versus enhanced content.

Evidence tier: historical source/diff studies, with commit and path existence rechecked in local Git during this backfill. No application build, dependency resolution, signing, installation or device execution was performed. Proposed checks above are acceptance criteria, not completed tests.
